reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents a step-by-step OneCoin registration and package-activation process that directs viewers toward account setup and payment, including paid upgrades costing thousands of euros linked to tokens and points. It also describes a transaction password for withdrawing money expected from the business, although registration is initially free and the sampled dashboard shows zero balances and an unregistered payment notice.

If you want to buy, for example, a box let's say 1000 that are going to select this one, 1000 to upgrade
This password will let us do all the transactions Either withdrawing or charge the money we will earn or we are going to take in this business

opening.argument: The presentation uses conditional, cautionary language rather than promising an outcome. Viewers are told that they need not buy a package immediately and that the account is free, while the registration process is presented as a demonstration account. That framing leaves the decision with the viewer and does not guarantee earnings, returns, or successful withdrawals. The material therefore reads as a cautious orientation to a platform, not an unequivocal deceptive solicitation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited package language shows that an upgrade option exists, but it does not establish that viewers were required to pay or were promised a return. The transaction-password statement describes a possible account function, not an actual withdrawal or guaranteed income. The dashboard evidence likewise shows an account interface, not a completed payment or realized loss.

citations.quote: the only thing you need to do now is have Your account is totally free
This password will let us do all the transactions Either withdrawing or charge the money we will earn or we are going to take in this business

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the account free does not neutralize the later solicitation. The material expressly instructs viewers how to purchase or upgrade packages, and the displayed packages include mining and cryptocurrency education language, daily OLP points, and prices in the thousands. A scam classification does not require proof that a payment or withdrawal already occurred.

citations.quote: the other part I mentioned here is for you to purchase your coupon update your package

opening.argument: This is most naturally understood as an operational tutorial. The title identifies it as a registration tutorial, and the narration walks through usernames, email, passwords, country selection, phone entry, verification, and dashboard navigation. It also explicitly describes the account as a demo account. Explaining how an interface works, including optional later features, is educational instruction; the recording does not establish that the presenter collected money, delivered an investment return, or verified the platform's claims.

citations.quote: How to Register on OneCoin Tutorial
In this video we'll see how to register correctly With a very simple way
this is nothing more is a demo account
Then select open

rebuttal.rebuttal: The tutorial format is not disproved by the fact that it includes package instructions. The narration separates account creation from later activation, says the account can remain free, and describes verification before discussing packages. Showing where a feature is located is not itself proof that the presenter is certifying a return or inducing an actual deposit.

citations.quote: the only thing you need to do now is have Your account is totally free
next, just click this button then says that his account has been verified
if you're ready if you want to buy this package

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional format is precisely how the promotion is made actionable. The video does not merely discuss a hypothetical interface: it gives step-by-step registration guidance, then explains how to select a package, enter payment or gift-code information, and activate it. The tutorial label does not change the substance of those instructions.

opening.argument: The available evidence is also consistent with ordinary commercial package sales and referral-style account administration. The account may be created for free, while a user who chooses to proceed can select among listed packages or use a gift code. The record does not show a required deposit, a guaranteed return, a completed payment, or money actually withdrawn. The dashboard instead displays zero-valued account fields, so the alleged financial outcome is not established by this video.

citations.quote: the only thing you need to do now is have Your account is totally free
if we are using a code, we can do it, we can select a gift code

rebuttal.rebuttal: A package menu and gift-code field are ordinary commerce signals unless the evidence proves a deceptive mechanism. Here, the narration says the account is free and presents purchasing as conditional. The cited transaction-password language does not show that money was earned, withdrawn, or guaranteed, and the dashboard does not demonstrate a completed transaction.

citations.quote: if You are not yet ready to buy any form package do not worry
This password will let us do all the transactions Either withdrawing or charge the money we will earn

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The commercial presentation goes beyond a neutral retail listing: the registration screen says users will be rewarded with tokens, while the package screen describes mining and cryptocurrency education and recurring daily points alongside high prices. The speaker also explains payment and activation steps. Those features support a paid return-oriented scheme even though this sample does not show a completed payment.
